item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I adore this. To death.

It really captures just how out of their league the UIU is supposed to be. I know Clef originally intended them to be a bit like bumbling X-files buffoons, but I like this interpretation much better. Incompetence will get you fired in the Feds. Sure you can be lazy and out of your depth, but if you actually don't do your job, you get axed. Here, it shows them - as a whole - able and willing to commit, but completely outclassed in a world that wants them dead and burned to ashes from mind lasers. Their lack of progress is due to the public consciousness seeing them as a joke and the fear that every bump in the dark is just the mind lasers powering up.

Even the speaker is awesome. He's experienced, but only so much as his situation will allow. He has no idea what half the stuff he finds actually does, but he's learned through trial and error what has the least chance of getting him killed. He's still out of his depth, but shows a cool head and the ability to learn with only scraps of information to work with. "Okay, the skippers don't want me doing this in this specific situation, so I'll try this next time instead." The guy might even get drafted by the Foundation, but I love him even more in the role he currently has.

I can even understand why he has the deagle with the bottomless clip. The Foundation can't find everything, so it stands the reason they'd throw the UIU a bone or two so they can do their own research and investigations. No use having the hired help be so completely fucked that'd get slaughtered easily. All the Foundation would need to do is scoop up whatever anomalies they deem important to confiscate.

Upvoted with extreme prejudice.

I liked the tale. I could imagine the new recruits (probably 3 or 4) sitting in a lecture theater listening to some ancient UIU veteran that gets no respect rambling on about stuff that they already know, rolling their eyes.

Then he ejects an impossible amount of bullets from the magazine, and everything changes… Good stuff. +1.

My Head Cannon for the UIU. Might conflict a bit with this tale, but there is no canon. Thank God.
hide wall of text

This I believe: The UIU employs fewer than 1000 people (exactly how many I know not). A comparison between their humble office and the "VAST with a capital V" resources of the Foundation is laughable. In fact, UIU has no idea that SCP even exists!

What the UIU does know is that even if anomalies were out there, there are people who hold wool over their eyes. They have never been the first responders to "Unusual Incidents", if there ever were any. The British, the French, almost certainly the Russians, and yes, the federal government of the United States, have kept them in the dark. Why? Because the keeping of secrets that jeopardize normalcy and the continuation of the human race is not to be the responsibility of a bunch of ill-motivated and/or incompetent federal police officers!

This perceived group or groups that are covering everything up are in reality the SCP, GOC, GRU-P (though not as much nowadays) and MIB. The first three need no introduction (See "Groups of Interest"). The MIB is not actually called the MIB. They are a US government agency with no real, consistent name that has been tasked with the protection of America and America's interests from anomalous events and items since the 1950's. They have the ultimate jurisdiction anywhere in America; they are the "men in black" of legend. Think the SCP, only with less resources and far less bureaucracy. Also, they're less accountable than the CIA, which is a scary thought.

Of course, all this isn't to say that the UIU can't be compelling. There is an elite, privately-funded group of brave souls who chase the truth. They meet in secret and are invisible, even to SCP. Several members are formerly or currently employed by UIU…..

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Though I'll apologize for yet again bumping this particular tale today, after having finished reading all the comments I felt I had to at least add one last bit to add to the whole mix regarding this tale. There's been a great hubub from several people, downvoting and getting quite angry indeed because they felt that this story severely violated their headcanon for the UIU. Quite a bit of attacking has been related to Kingreaper daring to, horror of horrors, make the UIU more then a cardboard cutout, and give some potential depth for any stories involving them.

Personally, I find this take on them amazing, and something more then fit for the site as a whole. There's only one bone that I have to pick with the people that so… boisterously defended the idea of the UIU being nothing but a bunch of ineffectual jokes: how does this remotely preclude that? They can still be utterly bungling, idiotic agents in any stories that they are involved in. They can be the butt of any jokes that a writer wants to play out. The UIU agent in question can be moronic, lazy, can STILL disbelieve that the paranormal is really out there; the human mind is able to deny quite a hell of a lot when it wants to, and even if someone went to this orientation, internally calling the 'infiniclip' some kind of hoax or trick and disregarding it is well within the realms of possibility.

This orientation doesn't mean that the group can't be the three stooges of any stories someone wants to make. It only means that there's more depth to them then has previously been explored. An agent doesn't have to be an idiot, they could be some good, honest guy that was thrown under the bus. They could be a previously lazy individual that, when exposed to the reality of the world, finds new purpose. They could be someone that, in their previous posting, had some major runin with the supernatural and had the poor sense to actually go and report it to their superiors. The initial idea isn't gone, this just all comes down to how you write them.

But that's the trick, isn't it? Who -has- written about them, exactly? Because I sure as heck haven't seen any of the people most strenuously assaulting the piece coming forward with their own work. And though that naturally doesn't mean much on its own, the one piece actually tagged with the UIU where it -IS- just a useless expy of the X-Files is at +4. This is, as of my upvote, +75.

Dr Clef made the initial idea of them being bumbling do-nothings, yes, but then he hasn't exactly seen fit to go and give them any actual attention, has he? The piece that is most true to the original source concept is, to put it mildly, not doing terribly well for itself. And it isn't as if this is someone trying to radically alter the Foundation, or the GOC, or any other major group. This isn't the author trying to shift MC&D into a loving, charitable organization. It is someone putting a new spin on a group that barely anyone gave a damn about before.

With this, Kingreaper has breathed new life into a group, keeping a core of what people want them to be - potential to bring an inept asshat into their worlds - while allowing them to be so very, very much more. It takes them from a flat, two dimensional joke to a group that, potentially, far more accurately represents a basic everyman than any foundation member ever can, whilst also allowing them the potential to stay a joke if the person reading about them, or writing about them, wants them to be.

That's true to an extent.

Personally I think it takes a particularly good writer to make a story where the main character is incompetent, as are all their immediate superiors.

But having such a group in the background of a story about someone else can make good comic relief.

Whereas a group that's in over its head and/or down on its luck, but is moderately competent, can fill the "everyman" role, which is much easier to write for.

So while you can make a good story with anything, making a good story centring on the truly incompetent version of the UIU is going to be a lot harder than basing it on the "in-over-their-heads" UIU.

item.content:encoded:
What do you do with the agent that arrests the diplomats wife - even if she DID deserve it?

Say I get a guy that just… coasts. He doesn't do anything WRONG, but he shows no initiative, won't extend himself, won't grow. And he's been tosed from job to job to job because there's never been any GOOD reason to can him.

What do you do with the guy that's just in the wrong place at the wrong time? Constantly.

The agent that was falsely named in a scandal?

How about the agent that has lost four partners in four years. It's NEVER his fault - but no one will team with him.

The burnout that refuses to take a medical discharge?

The reality (and good fiction) is that you often CAN'T just fire someone.

The agent that believes in Bigfoot and aliens and time travel and demons and magic and… oh, you have a spot for him?

These are just off the top of my head. An Amazon search can give you any number of stories about of a down on his luck cop.

The gun of many bullets being in their possession is fine to me too. They've got it only because someone tried to use it on one of their agents and its never been officially reported up the chain. The Foundation doesn't know they've got it (yet). It's not the sort of big and obvious item that instantly gets attention, its the sort of thing that turns up by chance. On this occasion chance dropped it into the UIU's hands and no one has noticed it yet. It'll probably get taken off them shortly.

Or maybe they are being allowed to keep it (unknowingly of course) as the sole bit of "evidence" they get to have to keep them chasing at shadows. After all if the UIU are occasionally useful then they have to be given something to keep them in roughly the same page. Its the sort of thing that is semi-useful without being flashy or overwhelming. The moment they try to use it to prove anything to anyone it gets taken away from them, but as long as all they do is use it as a prop for a "the truth is out there" speech then its effectively contained. It's the Foundation's way of keeping them on a leash, to be yanked as per requirement.

Random thought for those who downvote for UIU having an anomalous item: Maybe they won't have it for very long.

Acquisition and Containment isn't instant, even for very high priority items which this gun would not be. If it helps you integrate the tale into your head canon, assume that the speaker picked it up after an operation last night and won't have it or his memories of it by this evening. The tale is just a snapshot of a brief window of time when he gets to feel vindicated and not look like an idiot in front of the new recruits. Tommorrow morning, he will have to do it again for the first time and be back on the standard, "we are a bunch of losers chasing shadows that aren't there" party line again.

Just tossing the idea out there. I don't subscribe to the UIU as Keystone Cops vision, myself.
